variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Real-time ML inference is the production process of turning a live request or event into a model prediction within a strict latency deadline. A complete path usually retrieves fresh features, selects a model, runs inference, applies business rules, records telemetry, and returns or emits the result.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Request-response
pairs.detail: Return one decision before the caller's deadline.
pairs.explanation: Return one decision before the caller's deadline. Feature retrieval, queueing, inference, policy, and serialization all share that budget.

pairs.label: Event stream
pairs.detail: Consume durable events and emit predictions continuously.
pairs.explanation: Consume durable events and emit predictions continuously. Ordering, replay, state, and idempotent outputs replace synchronous response concerns.

pairs.label: Micro-batch
pairs.detail: Accumulate a small number of compatible requests to improve utilization.
pairs.explanation: Accumulate a small number of compatible requests to improve utilization. Set a maximum wait so throughput does not consume the product deadline.

pairs.label: Precompute or edge
pairs.detail: Serve a recent prediction near the caller when freshness and key cardinality permit.
pairs.explanation: Serve a recent prediction near the caller when freshness and key cardinality permit. Invalidation and versioned cache keys become correctness concerns.

variants.hint:
Request-response: Return one decision before the caller's deadline.

Event stream: Consume durable events and emit predictions continuously.

Micro-batch: Accumulate a small number of compatible requests to improve utilization.

Precompute or edge: Serve a recent prediction near the caller when freshness and key cardinality permit.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Real-time ML inference is the production process of turning a live request or event into a model prediction within a strict latency deadline. A complete path usually retrieves fresh features, selects a model, runs inference, applies business rules, records telemetry, and returns or emits the result.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: In-process
pairs.detail: Avoids a network hop but duplicates memory across replicas and loses entries on restart.
pairs.explanation: Avoids a network hop but duplicates memory across replicas and loses entries on restart. Use only for bounded, safe-to-recompute values.

pairs.label: Distributed memory
pairs.detail: Shares predictions or features across servers.
pairs.explanation: Shares predictions or features across servers. The cache is still a dependency with timeout, capacity, hot-key, and invalidation failure modes.

pairs.label: Edge cache
pairs.detail: Works for broadly reusable results whose privacy, model version, policy, and freshness can be encoded in a safe key.
pairs.explanation: Works for broadly reusable results whose privacy, model version, policy, and freshness can be encoded in a safe key.

pairs.label: No prediction cache
pairs.detail: Run inference when outputs depend on private, high-cardinality, rapidly changing, or non-deterministic inputs.
pairs.explanation: Run inference when outputs depend on private, high-cardinality, rapidly changing, or non-deterministic inputs. Optimize features and runtime instead.

variants.hint:

Edge cache: Works for broadly reusable results whose privacy, model version, policy, and freshness can be encoded in a safe key.

No prediction cache: Run inference when outputs depend on private, high-cardinality, rapidly changing, or non-deterministic inputs.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Real-time ML inference is the production process of turning a live request or event into a model prediction within a strict latency deadline. A complete path usually retrieves fresh features, selects a model, runs inference, applies business rules, records telemetry, and returns or emits the result.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: ETA or risk score
pairs.detail: Combine live context with durable entity features, use a bounded model call, and return a fallback estimate when fresh dependencies miss the deadline.
pairs.explanation: Combine live context with durable entity features, use a bounded model call, and return a fallback estimate when fresh dependencies miss the deadline.

pairs.label: Recommendation
pairs.detail: Generate a small candidate set before expensive ranking.
pairs.explanation: Generate a small candidate set before expensive ranking. Log exposure so clicks do not become an uncorrected feedback loop.

pairs.label: Fraud decision
pairs.detail: Use calibrated thresholds, rules, and human review around the model.
pairs.explanation: Use calibrated thresholds, rules, and human review around the model. Preserve idempotency and an auditable reason path for adverse actions.

pairs.label: Search ranking
pairs.detail: Run lexical retrieval, learned retrieval, ranking, and policy under separate budgets.
pairs.explanation: Run lexical retrieval, learned retrieval, ranking, and policy under separate budgets. Degrade by skipping stages instead of timing out the request.

Search ranking: Run lexical retrieval, learned retrieval, ranking, and policy under separate budgets.
